meta.name: MusicLinkd Design Tokens
meta.note:
v9.0 (2026-08-29) is a DELETION pass plus dual authoring, not an expansion. v8 documented a system whose live CSS had grown to 248 custom properties in one :root — 26 radius tokens, 29 spacing, 21 duration, 20 opacity, 14 type, 11 shadow — where every token past the 4-step core was a provable exact duplicate (--r-sm = 8px = --radius-1; --op-hover = 0.08 = --opacity-1; --el-1 = --shadow-1). Those aliases carried zero information and made the contrast between steps unreadable, which is the entire point of a 4-step exponential scale. v9 keeps ONE name per value. No scale may exceed 4 steps.

The second change is dual authoring: every token that differs between web and native now carries explicit $web / $android / $ios forms. This closes the real native gap — clamp() does not exist on Android or iOS, and native motion is spring physics rather than duration+bezier, so a single web-shaped value could never have been handed to a Compose engineer.

Also repaired here: 155 var() references in styleguide.html pointed at names that were never defined anywhere in the file (--white ×62 with no fallback, --surface-subtle ×26, --r-avatar ×14, --ease ×12, --text-2 ×7, --navy ×4, --ink ×3). Verified resolving to empty string on the deployed page, 2026-08-29. The names that represent real values (--white, --surface-subtle, --ink) are defined properly below; the rest were duplicates of existing tokens and are retired.

palette.$description: Governing visual rule, set by the brand owner 2026-08-29 against Apple Music / Shazam / SoundCloud / Instagram / Tinder: THE CHROME IS MONOCHROME, THE MEDIA CARRIES ALL THE COLOUR. Black, grey and white build every surface and control. Album art, studio photography, waveforms and profile imagery supply all saturation. Pink is a ~10-15% accent — state, selection, focus, brand mark — and is never a surface fill. Approximate budget: black ~60%, grey+white ~30%, pink ~10-15%.

removed.purple: #8B5CF6 and --purple-container #F3E8FF were live in styleguide.html's :root despite frontend/guide/README.md's Boundaries section explicitly forbidding purple brand tokens. Deleted.
removed.navy: #0D0B26 removed per the black/grey/white + pink palette rule. It was referenced by semantic.surface.navyHero and by webapp's theme-color meta tag; both move to foundation.color.ink.

darkMode.$description: Deliberately not built. The system is light-only and monochrome — that is a position, not a gap. v8's semantic.action.dark block is removed rather than left dangling. Revisit only on explicit instruction; when it happens the decision that must be made first is the dark elevation rule (Gestalt drops shadows for a 1px border, Material raises surface tint) — MusicLinkd has never made that call.

tokenBudget.$description: Enforced by scripts/build-tokens.mjs, which fails the build if the generated CSS exceeds the ceiling. Measured live on /guide/styleguide 2026-08-29 before this pass.
tokenBudget.$ceilingNote2: Raised 104 -> 108 on 2026-08-31 for foundation.weight (4 steps). This is a NET REDUCTION in hand-typed values, not sprawl: the four tokens replace 114 literal font-weight declarations that no single edit could reach. Adding them is what made the 700 -> 600 change one edit instead of a hundred and fourteen.
tokenBudget.$ceilingNote: Raised 66 -> 104 on 2026-08-30 after a full reconciliation against the supplied spec. The ceiling exists to stop DUPLICATE-value sprawl — the same 8px under six names, which is how the old system reached 248 — and every token added in this pass is a distinct value with a distinct job: 4 icon sizes, 4 avatar sizes, 2 elevation levels restored, 2 border widths, 3 semantic colours (info/disabled/scrim), 8 platform-fixed component dimensions, 2 layout constraints, 4 interaction values and 3 chrome insets. Twenty-two further spec entries were MAPPED onto existing tokens rather than emitted — see meta.tokenMap — which is the ceiling doing its job. The 4-step-per-scale rule is unchanged and still enforced.

gestaltSource.$description: Gestalt is REFERENCE ONLY, per frontend/guide/README.md — never a runtime dependency. v8 inlined its full scales into this file (17 spacing steps, 12 rounding, 11 duration); those are removed because they were being consumed as if they were MusicLinkd tokens. What survives from Gestalt is the 423 Apache-2.0 icons already extracted to musiclinkd-system/icons/.

scaleAudit.$description: Requested by the brand owner 2026-08-30: 'when I said I will restrict to just 4 families I believed in contrast/high difference and get better UX — please audit it.' Measured, not asserted. A step is judged PASS if each neighbour differs by >=1.5x, which is roughly where a difference stops being arguable at a glance.

pass.radius: 8/16/32 — 2.0x, 2.0x. Step 4 (9999) is functional, not a scale step.
pass.elevation: blur 3/12/24/32 — clearly separable at every step.

fail.size: 32/40/48/56 — 1.25x, 1.2x, 1.17x. Constant set, not a scale — Material's 48dp / iOS's 44pt touch-target floor rules out an exponential ramp here.
fail.type: 12/16/22/32 — 1.33x, 1.38x, 1.45x. Modular perfect-fourth ramp (1.33x), chosen for text — not a strict 1.5x scale by omission.

tokenMap.$description: Every dimension in the supplied spec that already had a home, recorded so 'is it missing?' has a checkable answer instead of a guess. These are MAPPED, not duplicated — emitting them would be new names for existing values, which is how the previous system reached 248 tokens.
tokenMap.--state-focus-ring: 2px --color-pink at 2px offset — one definition, in ml-core.css :focus-visible
tokenMap.--int-web-hover-transition: --duration-2 (200ms), aliased as --gesture-hover-transition because the spec names it
tokenMap.--sp-xs / -sm / -md / -lg / -xl / -2xl: --space-1 / -2 / -3 / -4; 24 and 48 have NO token by design — they are the midpoints an exponential scale deliberately omits
tokenMap.--r-card / -media / -pill / -avatar: --radius-3 (32, spec said 24 — changed to match the scale) / --radius-2 / --radius-4 / --radius-4
tokenMap.Font fallback: declared inside each --font-* value, not a separate token
tokenMap.Tabular numbers: a utility class .ml-tabular, not a token — it is a font-feature-settings switch, not a value

knownGaps.$description: Recorded rather than quietly skipped, per the brand owner's instruction that skipping is not allowed. Each has a reason.
knownGaps.breakpoints 767/1023/1440 — decision, no: The spec's four breakpoints were considered and NOT adopted, not overlooked. platform.windowSize keeps Material's 600/840 WindowSizeClass values because those are what Compose actually branches on, and the app is Android-first. Shipping web breakpoints that disagree with the native ones is the exact drift v9 removed. --layout-max 1440 is kept as a max-width, which is what the spec's 1440 figure really was.
knownGaps.density modes: Not implemented, as the spec itself notes.
knownGaps.Snackbar 4s/10s: Durations are behaviour, not design tokens — they belong to the toast controller, not the stylesheet. Documented in the toast section's prose instead.

color.$description: ONE COLOUR BOOK. 20 colours in a single group, merged 2026-08-30 on the brand owner's instruction — there was a second group (foundation.brandColor) and two books is how a team ends up picking from the wrong one. The separation is now carried by the NAME: brand* entries are expression-only (marketing, key art, covers, decks) and a product screen never reaches for them; everything else is the UI palette. Neutrals do the work; pink accents; four status colours. Any saturation beyond this comes from media, never from chrome.

ink.$description: Primary action AND primary text. The single darkest value — replaces --black, --text and the retired --navy.

white.$description: Card and sheet fill. Was referenced 62 times in styleguide.html and never defined — the single worst broken token in the system.

surface.$description: Subtle raised/sunken fill — search bars, inactive segments, skeletons. Absorbs both v8's --surface-alt (#F8F8FB) and --surface-2 (#F1F5F9), which were visually indistinguishable, and the 26 broken --surface-subtle references.

muted.$description: Secondary text, metadata, placeholder. Absorbs the 7 broken --text-2 references. Darkened from styleguide.html's #7D7D8E on 2026-08-29: that value measured 3.94:1 on --color-paper, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 floor for normal text, and it is the colour of EVERY piece of secondary copy in the app — so the whole app failed AA. #6E6E7D measures 4.89 on paper, 5.01 on white and 4.73 on surface.

pink.$description: Brand accent — focus ring, selection, active tab, brand mark, waveform progress. NEVER a surface fill and never the primary CTA.

pinkPressed.$description: Two jobs, one token. (1) Pressed/active state of an accent control. (2) The ONLY pink permitted for TEXT: the brand pink #EA4C89 measures 3.48:1 on paper and fails AA as text, while this measures 5.24. Rule: pink FILLS and marks use --color-pink; pink TEXT uses --color-pink-pressed. Darkened from #D93C77 (4.21, still failing) on 2026-08-29.

pinkContainer.$description: The one permitted tinted surface — accent chips, progress tracks. Used sparingly.

inkPressed.$description: Pressed state of a primary (black) control — lifts off pure black so the press is visible

brandWarmPink.$description: Brand pink. Hotter and more saturated than the UI accent #EA4C89, which stays what it is — see the palette note. EXPRESSION ONLY — never on a product screen.

brandBlack.$description: Brand black, faintly blue. Distinct from the UI --color-ink #0D0D0D, which is a true neutral. EXPRESSION ONLY — never on a product screen.

brandWhite.$description: The supplied swatch labelled White carried HEX #000000 against RGB 255 255 255 — contradictory. RGB and the swatch itself both say white, so #FFFFFF is used and the hex in the source artwork should be corrected. EXPRESSION ONLY — never on a product screen.

brandDarkGray.$description: EXPRESSION ONLY — never on a product screen.

brandLightGray.$description: EXPRESSION ONLY — never on a product screen.

info.$description: Informational badge — 'On Tour', 'Remote available'. Fourth status colour, added 2026-08-30 from the spec's Semantic Colors table where it was the one status with no token. 4.68:1 on white, passes AA as text.

disabled.$description: Inactive control borders and text. Distinct from --color-muted, which is LIVE secondary text at 5.01:1; this is deliberately below AA because disabled content is exempt from 1.4.3 and must read as unavailable.

scrim.$description: Backdrop behind drawers, sheets and modals. Value equals --color-ink at --opacity-3; named because every overlay needs it and deriving it at 9 call sites is how it drifts.

purple.$description: BADGES ONLY. Reinstated 2026-08-31 on the brand owner's explicit instruction, restoring styleguide.html v4's rule 'Pink=Brand. Black=Primary. Purple=Badges only.' NOTE: meta.palette.removed.purple records that this colour was deleted because frontend/guide/README.md's Boundaries section forbade purple brand tokens — that boundary is now superseded for this one scoped use, and README.md is updated to match. Purple is never a button, a link, a border or a surface, and carries no state meaning: it is not success, warning or error. It marks a badge as a CATEGORY label rather than a state, which is the job no existing status colour does.

space.$description: 4-step exponential (r=2). Identical on web (px) and native (dp).

3.$description: Card padding, default gap, screen gutter

1.$description: Chips, small controls, inline media thumbs

4.$description: Pill / full round — buttons, chips, avatars. Functional, not a scale step. Absorbs the 14 broken --r-avatar references: an avatar is radius-4.

size.$description: Control heights. Doubles as the touch-target scale — 3 IS the 48dp accessibility minimum and 4 IS the 56dp comfortable target, so no separate touch tokens are needed (v8 had both, duplicated).

1.$description: Chip, small button, compact icon button

3.$description: MINIMUM TOUCH TARGET. Android 48dp (Material), iOS 44pt (HIG). Primary buttons, list rows, tab bar items.

4.$description: Comfortable target — primary CTAs, FAB, player controls

weight.$description: 4 steps. Font weight was the one typographic axis with NO token — it was typed as a literal in 114 declarations (86 in ml-widgets.css, 19 in ml-core.css, 9 in scripts/build-guide.mjs), 56 of them the value 700, which is why nothing could be changed in one edit. 700 is deliberately absent from this scale: on 2026-08-31 the brand owner cut the heavy UI weight from 700 to 600, and leaving a 700 step would let it creep back. Step 4 (800) is display-only and is the sole weight above 600. Inter and Inter Tight are variable fonts, so every step is a real instance, not a synthesised bold.

3.$description: Semibold — the system's emphasis weight. Buttons, headings, badges, anything that used to be 700

4.$description: Display only — hero headlines and the one big number on a screen

type.$description: 4 steps. Web uses fluid clamp() between a 360px and 1440px viewport. NATIVE CANNOT — clamp() does not exist on Android or iOS — so each step carries an explicit sp ramp (Android) and a Dynamic Type style (iOS), both of which scale with the user's OS font-size setting. RULE: every step's web clamp MINIMUM equals its Android sp value (12/16/22/32). The preview is approved at phone width, so if the web minimum sat below the sp value the preview would be showing smaller text than the app will ever render — which is what happened before 2026-08-29 (web 10/14/20/28 against native 12/16/22/32; the caption measured 10.03px on screen). The clamp still scales UP toward the max on wider viewports, where there is no native counterpart to disagree with. Families: Inter Tight for display/titles, Inter for body/labels.

1.$description: Micro labels, captions, badges, metadata, timestamps

2.$description: Body copy, default UI text, list item titles

3.$description: Section headings, card titles, screen titles

4.$description: Display — hero headlines, now-playing track title, the one big number on a screen

font.$description: THREE families. Inter Tight sets display, Inter sets body, and Unica One — added 2026-08-30 on the brand owner's instruction — sets eyebrows, kickers and branded labels. Unica One is a display face with a single weight (400) and tall narrow caps; it is legible as a tracked uppercase label and illegible as body copy, so it is scoped to .ml-eyebrow and the brand blocks and must never be used below --type-1 or for running text. --font-mono is retired: it named 'JetBrains Mono', which was never loaded by any @font-face or Google Fonts link, so every use silently fell back to the generic monospace.

eyebrow.$description: Eyebrows, kickers, section labels, branded stat captions. ONE weight (400) — Unica One ships no others, so any weight declaration above 400 will be synthesised by the browser and will look wrong.

elevation.$description: FOUR levels, restored 2026-08-30 from the spec's Elevation Levels table. v9 had cut this to 2 on the argument that a flat monochrome system only needs one resting lift and one floating overlay. That was wrong in one specific way: a dropdown and a modal are both 'floating' but must not sit at the same depth, and a resting card and a hover card must differ or the hover reads as nothing. Blur ramps 3 -> 12 -> 24 -> 32, each step clearly separable. Android maps to Compose elevation dp; iOS to a shadow modifier.

1.$description: Cards, chips, resting surfaces. Prefer a --color-line border before reaching for this.

3.$description: FAB, side sheet, bottom sheet, mini-player

motion.$description: Dual-authored. Web gets duration + cubic-bezier; native gets spring physics, which is what Compose and SwiftUI actually animate with — a duration is not translatable to a spring and pretending otherwise was the core web-shaped assumption in v8. Four steps, matched pairwise.

1.$description: Press, ripple, toggle, chip select — must feel instant

2.$description: Icon change, colour change, hover lift, dismissal

3.$description: Sheet reveal, card lift, shared-element / container transform

$android.note: Spring.DampingRatioLowBouncy — the one step allowed to overshoot

4.$description: Entrance, modal, splash, expressive moments (the Shazam result reveal)

zIndex.$description: Web-only — native uses composition order, not a z scale. 4 tiers, exponential. Elements needing strict order inside one tier use a calc() offset off that tier rather than a 5th token.

1.$description: Persistent chrome — top bar, bottom tab bar

3.$description: Transient overlays — sheet, modal, and their scrims

icon.$description: FOUR icon sizes, added 2026-08-30 — the spec asked for exactly four and the system had none, so CSS carried raw 14/16/18/20/22/24/28/32 px at 49 call sites. These are OPTICAL constants, not an exponential scale: the library is drawn on 16- and 24-unit grids, so sizes that are not near-multiples of those grids render on half-pixels and blur. Ratios are 1.25/1.2/1.33 and that is correct here — see meta.scaleAudit.

1.$description: Inline with --type-1 caption text; also the native size of the 25 Gestalt 'compact' glyphs

2.$description: Default UI icon — buttons, fields, list rows, menu items

3.$description: Navigation and primary actions; the native grid of the other 398 glyphs

4.$description: Large — empty states, feature discs, illustration-scale marks

avatar.$description: FOUR avatar sizes. Distinct from --size-* (control heights) because an avatar is not a control and must not inherit a touch-target floor — a 24px facepile stack is correct and a 48px one is not. Radius is always --radius-4.

2.$description: List rows, comment threads, chat list

3.$description: Card headers, message bubbles, seller row

border.$description: Border widths, from the spec's Border Tokens table: 0 / 1 / 2dp = none / subtle / prominent. Only 1 and 2 emit — zero needs no token. Which COLOUR pairs with which width is a component decision and is documented in semantic.border rather than duplicated here: divider = 1px --color-line, focus = 2px --color-pink, selected = 2px --color-pink, disabled = 1px --color-disabled.

1.$description: Subtle — hairline card borders, dividers, list separators, input rest

2.$description: Prominent — focus ring, selected card or chip, featured tier

layout.$description: Page-level constraints. Gutters and gaps deliberately have NO tokens of their own: the spec listed --layout-gutter-mobile/tablet/desktop 16/32/32 and --layout-gap-sm/md/lg 8/16/32, and every one of those six values is already a --space-* step. Emitting them would be six new names for four existing values, which is exactly the duplication the token ceiling exists to stop. Mapping is recorded in meta.tokenMap.

max.$description: Page max-width at the widest layout. Not a breakpoint — see platform.windowSize.

measure.$description: Maximum readable line length for body prose. Answers the spec's 'Max Line Width'. In ch so it tracks the font, not the viewport.

component.$description: Values fixed by a platform contract rather than chosen by us, so they sit outside the 4-step scales on purpose. Every component dimension in the spec that DOES land on a scale is mapped instead of duplicated — button heights 32/40/48 are --size-1/2/3, input 40 is --size-2, chip 32 is --size-1, FAB small 40 / regular 56 are --size-2/--size-4, touch target 48 is --size-3. Only the values below have no scale home.

appbarSearch.$description: Search app bar — the spec's 56dp variant

appbarLarge.$description: Large app bar, profile pages and dashboard

drawerModal.$description: Modal navigation drawer — mobile hamburger menu

switchTrack.$description: Material 3 switch track width. Track HEIGHT is 32 = --size-1.

brand.$description: Identity rules, lifted from frontend/guide/brand/README.md so the catalogue can render them and that file stops being a second place the brand is defined.
brand.$positioningNote: Recovered 2026-08-31 from styleguide.html's Brand Identity block (v4.0), which the v9 rebuild dropped. It is the one line that says what the product IS, and the catalogue had been shipping voice and logo rules with no statement of position above them.
brand.voice: Clear, confident, creative, and professional. Avoid hype and generic marketplace language.

colourRoles.use: The brand signal. Intent, selection-in-progress, the one accent on a screen.
Every primary action and committed state. Black is the primary button, not pink.
Page ground. Chrome stays monochrome so media carries all saturation.

brand.$colourRolesNote: The old styleguide's rule read 'Pink=Brand. Black=Primary. Purple=Badges only.' The first two are carried over verbatim because they are still true and were nowhere in the v9 catalogue. PURPLE IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: there is no purple in foundation.color and no component uses one, so the badge rule described a colour the system does not have. Badges use the status colours or --color-ink. Recorded here rather than silently dropped, because a rule that vanishes without a reason is how the two colour books happened.
brand.$iconNote: styleguide.html specified 'Lucide icons, 1.75px stroke'. That is NOT the current library: the system ships 423 icons extracted from pinterest/gestalt, drawn on 16- and 24-unit grids as filled paths, not 1.75px strokes. The Lucide line is superseded, not an outstanding task.

display.use: Screen titles, hero headlines, numbers that matter

logoRules: Use real artist and business photography rather than initials, emoji, or illustrated avatars.
Keep source assets and exported delivery assets clearly named.
Place a mark on the ground it was drawn for — the on-dark lockups lose their counters on paper.
The wordmark set in Inter Tight (.ml-wordmark) is a type treatment, not a substitute for the artwork.

interaction.$description: Gesture thresholds. v8 recorded these as '$description: No MusicLinkd token — hardcoded in App.tsx'. The real values already existed in styleguide.html's --int-app-* block and had simply never been lifted into the source of truth. Doing that here is what lets SwipeDeckBlock and the bottom sheet stop hardcoding them, and gives Compose a number to match.

swipeThreshold.$description: Distance past which a swipe commits — sheet dismiss, swipe deck, row actions

dragThreshold.$description: Movement before a drag is recognised over a tap

pinchMin.$description: Minimum pinch-zoom scale — artwork and waveform detail views. App only; trackpad pinch on web is OS-level, not component-level.

tooltipDelay.$description: Hover dwell before a tooltip opens. WEB ONLY — a touch screen has no hover, which is why .ml-tip is documented as a desktop affordance and .ml-help exists for phones.

hoverTransition.$description: Hover state transition. Web only. EQUALS --duration-2 (200ms) and no longer emits: it was a second name for an existing value, which this file's own semantic block calls out as precisely how v8 reached 248 tokens. Kept here because the supplied spec names it, so 'is it missing?' still has an answer — see meta.tokenMap. Use --duration-2.

semantic.$description: ROLE DOCUMENTATION ONLY — deliberately emits no CSS custom properties. Every entry below whose value is a 1:1 alias of a foundation colour (action.primary = color.ink, surface.canvas = color.paper, text.primary = color.ink) would be a second name for the same value, which is precisely how v8 reached 248 tokens. On web, use the foundation token directly: --color-ink IS the primary action and the primary text. This block survives because the Compose and SwiftUI exports DO want role names (MLColor.actionPrimary), and because it records which foundation colour fills which role. media.* and haptic.* below are not aliases and do emit.

primary.$description: The CTA colour is BLACK, not pink (corrected 2026-08-16 by the brand owner and re-confirmed 2026-08-29)

accent.$description: Focus, selection, active state, brand mark — never a CTA fill

onMedia.$description: Text over artwork — always paired with the scrim gradient below, never placed on raw imagery

media.$description: The palette rule made operational. Media is the only element permitted to carry saturation, so it needs its own scrim and aspect contract to stay legible.

scrim.$description: Applied under any text laid over artwork

aspectCard.$description: Media card artwork — the one aspect that was hardcoded rather than tokenised

haptic.$description: v8 had three entries naming Android constants only, which is unusable for an iOS build and unusable on web. Each entry now maps all three platforms. Web uses the Vibration API and degrades silently where unsupported (iOS Safari has no Vibration API at all — that is expected, not a bug).

selection.$description: Chip select, tab change, waveform scrub detent

status.$description: Derived status pairs, NOT aliases. Each is a color-mix that was written inline across the stylesheets 26 times in total — success text alone appeared 8 times, success fill 4, error text 5. That is duplication of a DERIVATION, which the alias rule above does not cover and the ceiling exists to stop. Naming them once means a change to --color-success reaches every status surface. Info is deliberately absent: it is used once each way, so a token would be a name for a single call site.

errorText.$description: Rejected, failed, destructive — text/icon on that fill

successText.$description: Confirmed, available, complete — text/icon on that fill

warningText.$description: Pending, caution — text/icon on that fill

categoryBg.$description: CATEGORY badge container — purple. Not a state: success/warning/error say how something is going, this says what KIND of thing it is (genre, service type, role). That job had no colour, which is why screens were reaching for the accent pink and making category labels look like selection.

categoryText.$description: Category badge text/icon on that fill. Derived the same way as the status pairs, so a change to --color-purple reaches both halves and the contrast ratio is maintained by construction.

platform.$description: Where web and native genuinely differ. v8 recorded platform.app as 'consumesTokensFrom: Nothing yet' — these values now have real consumers in frontend/guide/system/ and are emitted into the Compose export.

safeArea.$description: Edge-to-edge is enforced for apps targeting current Android SDK levels and is the default on iOS, so insets are mandatory rather than optional. Web reads env(); native reads WindowInsets (Compose) / safeAreaInsets (SwiftUI). The px numbers are fallbacks only, for browsers with no env() support. TOP's fallback references --chrome-status-bar rather than repeating 24px: the two were the same number under two names, which is exactly the duplication the token ceiling exists to catch, and it left --chrome-status-bar referenced by nothing. BOTTOM's 16px stays a literal on purpose — it is a gesture-bar breathing space, not --chrome-nav-bar (48px, the three-button bar) and not a spacing step; mapping it onto either would be a category error.

windowSize.$description: Replaces v8's px breakpoints, which disagreed with themselves — styleguide.html declared 768/1024/1440 while the Gestalt block declared 576/768/1312, and neither is a size class. These are Material 3 WindowSizeClass widths, which is what Compose actually branches on and what foldables and tablets report.

medium.$description: ≥600dp — large phone landscape, small tablet, unfolded inner display

chrome.$description: System chrome we must reserve space for but do not draw. Android values are the framework defaults used as fallbacks when WindowInsets has not resolved yet; web scrollbar width matters because a 12px gutter appearing on overflow shifts a centred layout, which is a real bug we would otherwise chase at layout time.

navBar.$description: System navigation bar height fallback. EQUALS --size-3 (48px) and no longer emits — meta.tokenMap already records 'Nav height: --size-3 (48)', so emitting this was the map contradicting itself. The Compose/SwiftUI insets above are the real native answer; on web, use --size-3.

scrollbar.$description: Desktop scrollbar width. Web only — browser chrome is outside our control.
